s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with epigastric tenderness and radiating back pain
salient_findings: Progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
key_facts: No history of fever, chills, or previous similar pain
Current medications include insulin detemir, lispro, amlodipine, aspirin, atorvastatin, carvedilol, bumetanide, duloxetine, hydralazine, isosorbide mononitrate, and lisinopril
Vital signs: temperature 36.7 °C, blood pressure 200/100 mm Hg, heart rate 84 beats/min, respiratory rate 15 breaths/min
Dry mucus membranes and decreased skin turgor
Generalized abdominal tenderness worst in the epigastrium
Normal bowel sounds in all quadrants

shortlist.label: Acute Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated lipase level and epigastric pain radiating to the back

shortlist.label: Hypertriglyceridemia-induced Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated triglycerides and acute abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Medication-induced Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is taking multiple medications that can cause pancreatitis

shortlist.label: Peptic Ulcer Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Epigastric pain and history of pantoprazole use without relief

shortlist.label: Chronic Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of abdominal pain and elevated lipase level

raw.rationale: Elevated lipase level and generalized abdominal tenderness worst in the epigastrium are key indicators of acute pancreatitis

rejected.label: Hypertriglyceridemia-induced Pancreatitis
rejected.why: Triglycerides level is within normal range

rejected.label: Medication-induced Pancreatitis
rejected.why: No clear evidence of medication causing pancreatitis

rejected.label: Peptic Ulcer Disease
rejected.why: No evidence of peptic ulcer disease on imaging studies

rejected.label: Chronic Pancreatitis
rejected.why: Symptoms have only been present for one day, suggesting an acute rather than chronic condition
